query: How do I fix a toilet that keeps running?
answer:
Take the tank lid off and see where the water is going. The fix almost always comes down to one of two parts.

**1. Water spills into the overflow tube (the open pipe in the middle of the tank).** The fill valve or float is the problem [2]. Lower the float so the water stops about an inch below the top of that tube, or at the fill line if your tank has one [1]. Most valves have an adjustment screw or clip on top. Which way to turn it depends on the brand, so check the valve's markings first, then flush to test after each change [2].

**2. The water level is fine but the tank keeps refilling.** Water is probably leaking past the flapper, the rubber seal at the bottom of the tank. A chain that's too short or snagged can hold the flapper open, so adjust it by a link or two. If the flapper is cracked or warped, replace it. It's an inexpensive part [1].

If you can't tell which one it is, put a few drops of food coloring in the tank and wait about 15 minutes without flushing. If colored water shows up in the bowl, the flapper is leaking. That's a common trick, not something from the sources below.

If you've adjusted the float and checked the flapper and it still runs, the fill valve is likely worn out and needs replacing [1]. Shut off the supply valve behind the toilet before you swap any parts. If none of this stops it, call a plumber [1].
